title: Wallet adaptation done. The engine already sizes every quote to the cash in the wallet and caps one outcome at 25% of it. I fixed what did not scale: the prop cash reserves ( $90/$60 fixed) are now 60%/40% of the wallet, and the number of open parlays on one outcome (fixed at 2) grows by one for every $200 of wallet. I replayed the profile on four days of real market flow at wallets of $145, $300, $600 and $1,200: profit grows about in proportion to the wallet up to $600 (parlay pot per day $206, $378, $758, $1,326), and the supply of winnable parlays is still bigger than the cash even at $1,200, so no filter needs loosening when you add money. Loosening them actually spends the cash on slower, thinner parlays (about 25% less). I also built a cash-aware picker (as the wallet fills, quote only the parlays that return most per dollar locked per day) but left it OFF: it moved results by -7% to +10%, inside the noise, because the live filters already pick the capital-efficient ones. It is one switch if the flow thins. Honest scale: at my best edge estimate (+2.3% of pot) a $300 wallet is worth about $9 a day with big swings. Details: research/parlay_study_2026-11-20.md section 5.
